gates.title: Scalar/vector identity, notation and direction

authority_basis.claim_scope: Scalar/vector distinction, vector magnitude, direction and notation.

concepts.statement: A vector requires magnitude and spatial direction and obeys vector addition; a scalar does not.
Vector direction is meaningful only relative to a declared axis, bearing convention, or equivalent reference.

reasoning_sequence: Classify the physical quantity as scalar or vector.
Declare the direction reference before interpreting sign or angle.
Separate vector symbol from scalar magnitude.

misconceptions.bad_model: Any quantity described with a direction is automatically a vector.
misconceptions.repair: Require vector addition behaviour and spatial transformation, not directional wording alone.

gates.title: Vector addition, subtraction and resultant

authority_basis.claim_scope: Head-to-tail addition, subtraction as addition of the negative vector, and resultant meaning.

concepts.statement: The resultant is the single vector equal to the vector sum of all included vectors.
Vector subtraction is performed by adding the negative of the vector being subtracted.

conditions: Vectors expressed in a common frame

mandatory_elements: resultant from initial tail to final head

reasoning_sequence: Put all vectors in a common frame.
For subtraction reverse the subtracted vector.
Construct or compute the resultant and interpret its direction.

misconceptions.bad_model: Vector addition means adding magnitudes regardless of direction.
misconceptions.repair: Use head-to-tail geometry or components so direction participates in the sum.

gates.title: Component resolution and vector reconstruction

authority_basis.claim_scope: Orthogonal components, sign convention, magnitude and direction reconstruction.

concepts.statement: Component signs follow the declared axis directions and are not inferred from magnitude alone.
A vector must be reconstructable from its components into magnitude and quadrant-correct direction.

reasoning_sequence: Declare axes and sign convention.
Resolve the vector into signed components.
Reconstruct magnitude and direction from components as a reverse check.

misconceptions.bad_model: Components are always positive because magnitudes are positive.
misconceptions.repair: Components are signed projections; only the vector magnitude is non-negative.

gates.title: Forces as interactions with agent and receiver

authority_basis.claim_scope: Every force is an interaction exerted by an agent on a receiver.

concepts.statement: Every force in a Newtonian model is exerted by an identified agent on an identified receiver.

reasoning_sequence: Choose the receiver object or system.
List physical interactions crossing the system boundary.
Name each force by agent on receiver.

misconceptions.bad_model: An object contains or carries force as an intrinsic property.
misconceptions.repair: Name the external agent that exerts each force on the chosen receiver.

gates.title: System isolation and free-body diagrams

authority_basis.claim_scope: A free-body diagram shows only forces acting on the selected body/system.

concepts.statement: The body or system must be selected before deciding which forces belong on its free-body diagram.

reasoning_sequence: Select one body or system.
Identify interactions crossing its boundary.
Draw only forces acting on that selected system.
Check every arrow has a physical agent.

misconceptions.bad_model: Both members of a Newton third-law pair belong on one body's free-body diagram.
misconceptions.repair: An FBD contains forces on the selected body only; the partner force acts on the other body.

gates.title: Inertia, inertial frames and equilibrium

authority_basis.claim_scope: Zero net force implies zero acceleration in an inertial frame, not necessarily zero velocity.

concepts.statement: Mechanical equilibrium means zero acceleration because the net external force is zero; velocity may be nonzero and constant.

reasoning_sequence: Use the FBD to obtain the vector net force.
If net force is zero conclude acceleration is zero.
Keep constant nonzero velocity as a valid equilibrium motion state.

misconceptions.bad_model: Equilibrium means no forces act or the object must be at rest.
misconceptions.repair: Equilibrium requires vector cancellation of forces and zero acceleration, not absence of forces or zero velocity.

gates.title: Newton's second law axis-wise

authority_basis.claim_scope: Net external force equals mass times acceleration for constant mass, resolved consistently by axis.

concepts.statement: Newton's second law applies to the vector sum of external forces on the selected system, not to any one force in isolation.

reasoning_sequence: Select system and draw a complete FBD before equations.
Choose axes and resolve forces only after the FBD is physically complete.
Write net-force equations axis-wise for the same system.

misconceptions.bad_model: Any named force can be set equal to ma without summing all external forces.
misconceptions.repair: Start from the complete FBD and form the signed net force on each axis.

gates.title: Newton's third law on distinct bodies

authority_basis.claim_scope: Interaction-pair forces are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.

concepts.statement: The two forces in a Newton third-law pair act on two different bodies and therefore never cancel on one body's FBD.

symbol_bindings: F_A_on_B: force by A on B
F_B_on_A: force by B on A

reasoning_sequence: Identify one interaction between two bodies.
Name each force by agent and receiver.
Place each partner force on the FBD of its own receiver.

misconceptions.bad_model: Action and reaction cancel because they are equal and opposite.
misconceptions.repair: They act on different receivers; cancellation is meaningful only after selecting a common system containing both bodies.

gates.title: Normal contact force

authority_basis.claim_scope: Normal force is a contact constraint force perpendicular to the surface and is not generally equal to weight.

concepts.statement: Normal force is determined by the contact constraint and other force components; it equals mg only in special configurations.

symbol_bindings: F_normal_axis: signed force components normal to surface

reasoning_sequence: Draw the FBD without assuming the value of N.
Choose the surface-normal axis.
Use the normal-axis dynamics/constraint to solve N.

misconceptions.bad_model: The normal force is always equal to mg.
misconceptions.repair: Solve the surface-normal force balance/dynamics from the actual FBD.

gates.title: Tension and ideal-string constraints

authority_basis.claim_scope: Tension modelling depends on string/pulley assumptions and is not generally equal to a hanging weight.

concepts.statement: Equal tension across ideal massless string segments is a model consequence, not a universal fact for every string/pulley system.

reasoning_sequence: Declare the string/pulley model.
Draw separate FBDs for the bodies.
Apply the kinematic constraint and Newton equations consistently.

misconceptions.bad_model: Tension in a moving hanging body is automatically equal to mg.
misconceptions.repair: Use the body's acceleration in its Newton equation; T=mg only when the relevant acceleration is zero.

gates.title: Static and kinetic friction

authority_basis.claim_scope: Static friction adapts up to a limiting value; kinetic friction applies after sliding under the stated model.

concepts.statement: Static friction takes the value needed to prevent relative sliding up to its limiting value, rather than always equalling that limit.

reasoning_sequence: Decide whether surfaces stick or slide.
Determine the required friction from dynamics when sticking.
Compare with the static limit before switching to kinetic friction.

misconceptions.bad_model: Static friction is always mu_s N.
misconceptions.repair: Treat mu_s N as the maximum available static friction, not its automatic value.

gates.title: Connected-body systems and constraints

authority_basis.claim_scope: Connected-body problems require consistent system choices, internal/external force accounting and kinematic constraints.

concepts.statement: A multi-body problem may be analysed body-by-body or as a combined system, but internal/external force accounting must match the chosen system.

symbol_bindings: F_external: forces external to chosen combined system
conditions: Bodies share the declared acceleration constraint

mandatory_elements: separate-body FBDs or explicit combined boundary

reasoning_sequence: Declare whether analysis is separate-body or combined-system.
Draw compatible FBDs/system boundary.
Apply the kinematic constraint before solving the coupled equations.

misconceptions.bad_model: An internal force may be dropped even when analysing only one member body.
misconceptions.repair: Internal-force cancellation applies only after the relevant bodies are included in the same chosen system.

gates.title: Projectile launch-state component model

authority_basis.claim_scope: Projectile launch velocity is resolved into horizontal and vertical components in a declared inertial frame.

concepts.statement: After launch in the standard no-drag model, horizontal and vertical motion share one state but have different acceleration components.

reasoning_sequence: Declare the observation frame and axes.
Resolve launch velocity into signed components.
Apply the standard acceleration model only after the frame is fixed.

misconceptions.bad_model: Gravity cancels or changes the inherited horizontal launch component in the no-drag model.
misconceptions.repair: Gravity contributes vertical acceleration only; horizontal velocity remains constant in the standard model.

gates.title: One event clock for 2D projectile motion

authority_basis.claim_scope: Horizontal and vertical component equations describe the same particle at the same elapsed time.

concepts.statement: The x and y component equations refer to the same projectile and therefore use the same elapsed time for a given event.

symbol_bindings: t_x: time used in horizontal relation
t_y: time used in vertical relation
t_event: elapsed time to the same event

reasoning_sequence: Name the physical event being solved for.
Define one time origin.
Use the same event time in horizontal and vertical equations.

misconceptions.bad_model: Horizontal and vertical motions can use different times for the same projectile event.
misconceptions.repair: Both component descriptions are coordinates of the same state at one elapsed time.

gates.title: Launch from a moving source: frame conversion before projectile motion

authority_basis.claim_scope: Object velocity in the ground frame equals object velocity relative to the moving source plus source velocity in the ground frame under Galilean kinematics.

concepts.statement: Each velocity is named by moving object and observation frame before vectors are combined.
At release the object retains the source translational velocity contribution in the ground frame; release does not erase it.

symbol_bindings: v_object,ground: object velocity in ground frame
v_object,source: object velocity relative to source
v_source,ground: source velocity in ground frame

reasoning_sequence: Name the observation frame before using any velocity.
Convert the release velocity into the chosen frame by vector addition.
Only then resolve/use the ordinary projectile model with one post-release clock.
Verify by inverse frame conversion and the zero-source-speed limit.

misconceptions.bad_model: Once the ball leaves the moving source it loses the source's horizontal velocity contribution.
misconceptions.repair: Velocity is continuous through release under the model; gravity changes the vertical component but does not cancel inherited horizontal motion.
